title: Niccolò Ferducci to Ferdinand I, Fiume, 19 July 1532 (catalogue 498): eight nomenclator groups in a clear Italian letter

steps.what: Table of groups built from the contemporary glosses of 2-2-9 and 2-2-24 and frozen.
Frozen table applied to 2-2-19; all eight groups read.
No conflict between the two glossed letters; 6/6 agreement with the 1542 table (catalogue 499); month and year confirmed by the archival dockets "1532. 19/7".
Catalogue, Cryptiana, web, Gévay: no earlier reading.
PR review on merge (Claude Opus 5.5 for Daniel Bourdeau): method changed from external key to adjacent plaintext (the glossed letters are siblings in the same bundle); the glosses credited.

validation.notes: eight nomenclator groups in one letter, each value attested in the glosses of the sibling letters 2-2-9 and 2-2-24; too short for the letter-model test

texts.label: Ferducci to Ferdinand I, Fiume, 19 July 1532 (HHStA Türkei I 2-2-19)
texts.summary: A spy’s letter from the Ragusa network during Süleyman’s campaign: written in clear, it enciphers only eight words — names of people and places, the date and the signature. Once these groups are read, it reveals a plan: to seize the French ambassador at sea on his way back from the sultan.

reading_review.note: reading.md read paragraph by paragraph against translation.md: every sentence is coherent Venetian Italian and the eight code values fit their clauses (dal loro servitore [Martino Lucio], el bregantino da [Ragusa], [l'ambasciatore] de [Francia], Datta [S. Vito] a di 19 [luglio] [1532]). The only weak spots are four doubtful words of the clear hand (Lanbergher, a peschara, a divotione, ve se avisara); _check_reading's 0.64 counts the bracketed code values as holes.

prior.where: Catalogue 498 open; Cryptiana and web search (27 Oct 2026); not in Gévay, Urkunden und Actenstücke.
